data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: PRECIOUS-Tech rout drives gold to one-year low, white metals sink deep into oversold zone
data.description:
* Gold falls below key level of $4,000/oz

* Silver slides below $50/oz for the first time in 11 months

* Palladium slumps below $1,000/oz

* RSI for silver, platinum, palladium is in oversold territory

(Adds fresh analyst comment, performance of three white metals relative to gold, graphics)

By Noel John and Polina Devitt

Oct 30 (Reuters) - Gold prices hit their one-year low on Friday while white precious metals silver, platinum and palladium slid deep into technically oversold territory, as tech shares slumped amid worries that AI spending may not deliver sufficient returns.

Spot gold fell 3.1% to $3,897.09 an ounce by 11:47 a.m. ET (1547 GMT) - its lowest level since October 2025 - while silver dropped 6% to $49, breaking below $50 for the first time in 11 months, and palladium slid below $1,000.

"The sky is falling," said independent metals trader Tai Wong. "Metals will not be able to escape the gravity well of a nasty stock correction. Earnings have been the foundation of the AI rally and now that pillar is showing some cracks."

Friday's sharp fall in technology stocks may have led to forced selling of safe-haven assets, such as gold, and margin calls, analysts at Commerzbank said in a note, adding that they expected a recovery in precious metals ahead.

Gold is down 30% since hitting a record high of $5,595 in January due to bets on rates staying higher for longer and is currently under pressure from muted demand in Asia. Analysts, however, say central bank demand tends to strengthen whenever gold is below $4,000.

Meanwhile, the three white precious metals lack the support that gold has received in recent years from purchases by central banks and safe-haven investment demand.

This week's 7% to 9% fall in silver, platinum and palladium, compared with a 2% decline in gold, took their Relative Strength Index deeply into the "oversold" zone for the first time in three years, signalling the strength of current bearish momentum.

"What is particularly troublesome for the white metals is that the downturn has been grinding and relentless rather than a sharp spike that is quickly recovered," Wong said.

Silver was increasingly viewed as an industrial growth-dependent commodity. HSBC said industrial and jewellery demand for silver was falling, with the average price expected at $64 per ounce in 2027.

To buy a single ounce of gold, one currently needs 79 ounces of silver , the most in 11 months, compared with 46 ounces in January, when silver hit a record high of $122.

From a historical perspective, silver still has room to fall further vs gold: this ratio, according to consultancy Metals Focus, averaged 82 in 2020 to 2025.

Platinum and palladium touched their lowest levels in 13 and 17 months respectively, with palladium slipping below $1,000 an ounce and the gold-platinum ratio climbing to 2.7, the highest since mid-2025.

Platinum was last down 4% at $1,434, while palladium lost 3% to $977 under pressure from worries about auto sector demand.

(Reporting by Noel John and Polina Devitt; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks fall on AI cash burn worries while bonds rally with oil
data.description:
(Updates prices to early US afternoon)

* Intel ( INTC ) shares plunge 28% and Amazon ( AMZN ) falls 1.9% after results show AI investment burns cash

* Benchmark 10-year Treasury yield falls 4.36 basis points to 4.945% as investors seek safety

* MSCI ( MSCI ) global stock index drops 1.38% while Nasdaq slides 2.61% by early US afternoon

By Sinéad Carew and Iain Withers

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - A sharp selloff in Wall Street's tech shares pushed MSCI's ( MSCI ) global index down more than 1% on Friday, sending investors to the safety of US bonds on fears that hefty cash-burning AI investments may not deliver sufficient returns.

Shares in chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) plunged 28% and Amazon ( AMZN ) shares were off 1.9% after their results each showed they burned through cash while investing heavily in AI-related development. Intel ( INTC ) also said PC demand had slowed, and that it could persist through next year.

Shares in Google parent Alphabet, after falling 12.6% on Thursday, extended losses on Friday. Its massive AI spending turned the company cash flow negative while its search business faced stiff competition.

"It's really been a horror show this morning and the real villain is AI spending," said Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera, saying the heavy cash burn and elevated capex are prompting questions about whether the AI returns will "justify the outlays."

Goldman also said pressure from rising oil prices due to more attacks in the Middle East and concerns about a hack at Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, added to the gloom. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrency prices fell.

Outside tech, other sectors were holding up, particularly energy, which rose following results from Exxon Mobil and Chevron ( CVX ). The oil majors posted strong profits due to big refining margins driven by supply disruptions from Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and the US-Israel war on Iran. Shares rose 1.3% and 3%, respectively.

On Wall Street at 12:09 p.m. ET (1609 GMT), the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 384.61 points, or 0.73%, to 51,957.95, the S&P 500 fell 124.20 points, or 1.61%, to 7,595.93 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 684.06 points, or 2.61%, to 25,500.67.

MSCI's ( MSCI ) gauge of stocks across the globe fell 15.62 points, or 1.4%, to 1,117.00.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.46%.

In currencies, the yen headed for a third daily gain on Friday after the Bank of Japan held rates steady but revised up its inflation forecast, while a fresh wave of selling in AI shares triggered demand for non-dollar safe havens.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.03% to 101.85, with the euro down 0.07% at $1.117.

Against the Japanese yen, the dollar weakened 0.2% to 157.37.

Bitcoin fell 1.80% to $77,424.37.

US Treasuries rose, putting benchmark 10-year yields on track for their biggest monthly decline since late 2023, as the tech-stock selloff pushed investors into safe havens.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 4.36 basis points to 4.945% while the 30-year bond yield fell 0.69 basis points to 5.3221%.

The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 5.4 basis points to 4.602%.

Oil prices were on track for a fourth straight monthly gain. Traders are bracing for a potential escalation in the US-Iran conflict after the US midterm elections. The war has lingered for eight months without a resolution, and on Friday, a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked, highlighting the ongoing supply risks.

US crude rose 2% to $104.09 a barrel and Brent rose to $117.58 per barrel, up 2.4% on the day.

Precious metals fell. Gold dropped to a one-year low on Friday and silver slid below $50 an ounce for the first time since November 2025 as higher energy prices and persistent inflation concerns strengthened expectations that US interest rates will stay high.

Spot gold fell 3% to $3,901.83 an ounce. Spot silver fell 5.9% to $49.27 an ounce.

(Reporting by Sinéad Carew in New York, Iain Withers in London and Tom Westbrook and Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by Tom Hogue, Clarence Fernandez, Stephen Coates, William Maclean, Chizu Nomiyama and David Gaffen)

data.title: Fed's Musalem says a rate hike is needed 'soon'
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Friday he sees an imminent need to raise interest rates to deal with ongoing high levels of inflation.

"I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said in the text of a speech to be presented at an event held by the Shadow Open Market Committee, a group that takes stock of Fed actions and policies.

"Incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later," he said, adding that "moving sooner in smaller steps while inflation expectations are anchored has a better chance of succeeding without adverse impact on the labor market or economic growth."

Musalem said that inflation remains too high relative to the 2% target with ongoing risks to the upside, and added that it was unlikely to ease absent Fed action. He noted that monetary policy is not in a position to lower inflation at the current moment.

"I believe that monetary policy and financial conditions remain accommodative. Financial conditions tightened recently," Musalem said.

The Fed left its policy rate unchanged in the 3.75%-4.00% range after a meeting this week, as had been widely expected. The Fed raised rates in September, and financial markets expect another increase in short-term borrowing costs at the December meeting.

Musalem does not currently have a vote on the Fed's policy-setting committee, but will be a voter in 2027. Ahead of this week's policy meeting, Musalem had expressed support for higher rates to deal with high price pressures, in an economy where thus far, financial conditions are not providing the restraint needed to bring inflation back to the goal.

Two Fed policymakers dissented this week in favor of a rate hike. 

"I'm encouraged by the progress we've made in a short period of time" on lowering inflation, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said in a press conference after this week's meeting, while acknowledging that the central bank had not yet achieved price stability.

Warsh, who has been reluctant to provide guidance about the interest rate outlook, did not say what he thought the Fed would do at the December 8-9 policy meeting.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: FOREX-Yen gains after BOJ holds rates, dollar slips
data.description:
* BOJ leaves main rate unchanged

* Yen on track for third daily gain

* Dollar index slips but on track for second monthly gain

* Euro headed for monthly loss versus dollar

(Updates prices throughout, adds analyst comment)

By Amanda Cooper and Chibuike Oguh

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - The yen was on track for a third consecutive daily gain on Friday after the Bank of Japan left rates unchanged and upgraded its inflation outlook, while declining US Treasury yields weighed on the dollar.

The BOJ left its main rate at 1.25% in a widely anticipated move, but stressed that its policy has entered a new, more hawkish phase open to raising rates once every few months.

The yen strengthened to a high of 157.89 per dollar, set for a 0.11% gain in October.

The BOJ wraps up a week of central bank decisions, with the European Central Bank, the US Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand all leaving interest rates unchanged as they bide their time amid stubborn inflation and tightening financial conditions.

"The market is a little disappointed in the BOJ," said Joseph Trevisani, senior analyst at FXStreet. "The yen is a little bit stronger today but not as strong as it has been. We still have the Fed bias countering what the BOJ is doing."

The euro was down 0.17% at $1.1163 and was headed for a second straight monthly loss in October. It hit its lowest since May 2025 on Thursday, after the ECB left rates unchanged and indicated higher bond yields had tightened financial conditions, initially prompting traders to lower their expectations for a hike in December.

The Bank of England and the Reserve Bank of Australia will be in focus next week.

Sterling strengthened 0.14% to $1.3394. The Australian dollar strengthened 0.1% versus the greenback to $0.7034.

AI WORRIES

When investors seek out safe-haven assets, the dollar is often a beneficiary. But on Friday, the drag from a decline in Treasury yields was stronger. Results from Alphabet, Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) this week have rekindled worries about AI spending, which triggered a selloff in tech stocks on Friday.

The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six others, edged lower by 0.02% at 101.86. It has risen 0.39% in October, up for a second straight month.

The euro has found some support from the pressure that the AI-led selloff has put on the dollar, but with euro zone economic growth lagging that of the United States, this strength may soon dissipate, according to Barclays currency strategist Lefteris Farmakis.

Elsewhere, bitcoin was down 1.79% at $77,430.45, as investors pulled money from digital assets, after hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in the biggest crypto heist on record.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh in New York; Editing by Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

data.title: Chinese wireless firm Quectel accuses Telit of smear campaign in US lawsuit
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - Chinese wireless device manufacturer Quectel sued rival Telit on Friday, accusing it of a disinformation campaign that harmed Quectel's customer relationships and led the Pentagon to add it to a list of companies allegedly aiding Beijing's military.

Telit made and promoted false and misleading claims that Quectel's modules operate in a way that allows manipulation by the Chinese government, according to the lawsuit, filed in US District Court in the Southern District of Florida. 

Quectel is a leading supplier of Internet of Things (IoT) modules and Boca Raton, Florida-based Telit is a competitor.

"Rather than competing on the merits of their products, Telit engaged in a sophisticated and widespread disparagement campaign to exploit geopolitical concerns surrounding Chinese technology companies," Quectel said in its complaint.

Telit, which operates as Telit Cinterion, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Telit IoT Solutions is the named defendant. 

The Pentagon added Quectel in January to its list of companies it says work with China's military. The company sued the Pentagon in May, denying the allegation and saying it was causing it serious economic harm. The lawsuit is ongoing.

The US Department of Defense is barred from procuring goods, services or technology from companies on the list.

Quectel sued Telit on Friday for commercial disparagement, false advertising, cybersquatting, unfair competition and deceptive and unfair trade practices. The lawsuit says a Telit employee registered a quectel.us domain name and the company used it to redirect traffic to a disparaging Wikipedia page.

"Quectel cannot remotely control its IoT modules sold in the United States, send or receive data to and from those modules, or remotely deploy firmware-over-the-air updates to them," the lawsuit said. "Yet Telit promoted these false allegations while presenting itself to customers as a safer 'Western' alternative."

(Reporting by Karen Freifeld; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria)

data.title: Televisa expects AT&T purchase to strengthen position, debt will increase
data.description:
MEXICO CITY, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Mexico's Grupo Televisa said on Friday that the purchase of AT&T Mexican unit will materially strengthen its competitive position while the net debt will rise.

The $2 billion deal, pursued as a 50/50 joint venture with Fintech Holdings, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 pending regulatory approvals, creating a venture with about 24 million wireless subscribers.

-- Combined assets would also include 5.7 million broadband and 6.3 million video subscribers, Grupo Televisa co-CEO Alfonso de Angoitia said at an earnings call with analysts.

-- Televisa's net debt to EBITDA is expected to rise to 1.9 times after the deal, from 1.6 times at the end of the third quarter, he added.

-- Each partner will contribute $400 million in equity, with the remaining $1.2 billion funded through a five-year non-recourse loan.

-- Combined annual revenue would reach around $8 billion, roughly 23% of Mexico's telecom market.

-- The acquisition, "positioned us very well to consolidate our undisputable position as the second largest telco operator in our country," the executive said.

-- On Thursday, the world's largest producer of Spanish-language posted a return to profit in the third quarter, as softer revenue were offset by lower financial and tax expenses.

-- The acquisition of AT&T Mexico, which ended 2025 with revenue of 85.4 billion pesos and operating income of 1.4 billion pesos, marks Televisa's second attempt to enter the competitive telecom sector, after an unsuccessful effort between 2012 and 2014.

(Reporting by Raúl Cortés Fernández; Editing by Aida Pelaez-Fernandez)

data.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record heist blamed on North Korea
data.description:
SINGAPORE/PARIS/BOSTON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.

Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets. 

The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.

Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

"We NEVER use any customer funds, so they are not impacted," Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in a post on X.

Teng described the breach as a "complex attack" that was not carried out by one person and included a compromised laptop as well as malicious software designed to delete traces and evidence of its activity as it went along, "making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate."

The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, internet-connected wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said.

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

'BIGGEST HACK IN HISTORY'

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. 

The bulk of the Binance heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.

"TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in an analysis on its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible.

"This incident is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind," British blockchain analysts Elliptic said.

North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to US and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts.

North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.    

Binance is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Secret Service (USSS), a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.

The FBI said it was "aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps." 

The USSS did not respond to an emailed request for comment.

Abu Dhabi's Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance's main operating licence, said it was "engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident". 

"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said, as crypto prices fell broadly.

Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 6.2% over the past 24 hours at $702, according to CoinMarketCap, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.

SECURITY IMPLICATIONS

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group.

Investor Michael Saylor, among Bitcoin's most prominent supporters, said in a post on X that he expected Binance to "deliver" on ensuring no customers suffered losses. "Our industry will learn from this incident, strengthen security, and emerge stronger and more resilient," he wrote on Friday. 

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.

Abu Dhabi-backed investment group MGX became a minority investor in Binance last year. MGX declined to comment. 

(Reporting by Tom Westbrook, Ankur Banerjee and Rae Wee in Singapore, Summer Zhen in Hong Kong, Rocky Swift in Tokyo, Vallari Srivastava and Anusha Shah in Bengaluru and Mrinmay Dey in Mexico City, Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris, Tom Wilson in London, AJ Vicens in Detroit and Lawrence Delevingne in Boston; Writing by Scott Murdoch and Tom Westbrook. Editing by Stephen Coates, Mark Potter, Elisa Martinuzzi and Tommy Reggiori Wilkes)

data.title: TREASURIES-US bond yields fall as tech-related stock selloff intensifies
data.description:
* Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) weigh on stocks

* 10-year yield on track for biggest monthly fall since 2023

* Nasdaq down more than 2% early

(Updates to late US morning)

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Harry Robertson

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US Treasuries rose on Friday, putting benchmark 10-year yields on track for their biggest monthly decline since late 2023, as a sharp selloff in technology-related stocks added to concerns about AI spending and pushed investors into the safe-haven asset.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury was last down at 4.945%, set to fall about 35 basis points in October, its biggest monthly drop since December 2023.

The Nasdaq opened at its lowest level in more than two months, after Amazon's ( AMZN ) aggressive AI spending plan and Intel's ( INTC ) cash burn warning fueled investor concerns about the rising costs of the AI buildout.

The rally in US Treasuries prices in recent weeks has halted a sharp selloff that had pushed yields to multi-decade highs as investors fretted about rising energy costs and rising government debt.

"The last few weeks have just been an absolute sentiment shift," said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US rates strategy at TD Securities in New York. "The risks have really started to re-emerge, whereas a few weeks prior to that, everything was viewed as an upside risk to rates."

"The move lower (in yields) in the last few weeks has been more on expectations that you would get a moderation in growth dynamics, a moderation in AI," among other factors, he said. "To some extent, for rates investors, this is a question of whether the AI jitters persist or whether this is just a bump in the road on the way to rates remaining higher for longer."

AMAZON AND INTEL SHARES BOTH FALL

Amazon's ( AMZN ) shares were down 2.2% in early trading after the company reported a sharp cash outflow and another increase in spending, while chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) was down about 28% after warning that it would burn cash this year. An index of semiconductor firms was down 6.3%.

Yields also fell on Thursday after Alphabet's shares fell on disappointing results. At the same time, data showed September consumer spending accelerating, and the US economy growing at its fastest pace in a year.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last down 4.4 bps at 4.945%. The yield on the 30-year bond was down 1.3 bps at 5.316%.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes, seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at 33.3 bps.

The two-year US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was down 4.8 bps at 4.608%.

The breakeven rate on five-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) was last at 2.483% after closing at 2.469% on October 29.

The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate was last at 2.351%, indicating the level at which the market sees average annual inflation for the next decade.

data.title: Empresas Polar welcomes Ricos Products, originator of concession nachos, to its family of companies

Two family-built food companies join forces; Ricos will remain headquartered in San Antonio under its current management team

SAN ANTONIO, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Empresas Polar, a family-owned Venezuelan food and beverage company founded in 1941, today announced that its subsidiary, Alimentos Polar International, Inc. ("Alimentos Polar"), has acquired Ricos Products Co. ("Ricos"), a fifth-generation, family-owned San Antonio company and a leading marketer and supplier of nacho cheese sauce, chips, popcorn, and other products to retailers and concession stands worldwide.

Ricos' operations and management team will remain in place, and the company will continue to be headquartered in San Antonio. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

"Today marks an exciting new chapter in the Ricos story. Our family is very proud to have run a successful five-generation family business for over a century," said Tony Liberto, family member and Chief Executive Officer of Ricos. "In Empresas Polar we found the right steward for Ricos: a company that shares our heritage as a family-built food company and our passion for the Ricos brand. Their long-term commitment will allow us to accelerate our growth and innovation, expand our reach and keep delivering high-quality products to our customers. Our family would like to thank our loyal business partners, customers and, most importantly, our employees, who have made Ricos what it is today."

"Ricos is a true American original, and we have tremendous respect for what the Liberto family has built over five generations," said Lorenzo Mendoza, [President and CEO] of Empresas Polar. "As a family-owned company ourselves, we understand the importance of preserving that legacy. Our commitment is to build on everything that makes Ricos special - its people, its San Antonio roots, and the quality and traditions its customers have come to trust - while investing in the company's continued growth and bringing its products to even more consumers around the world. We are proud to welcome Ricos to the Empresas Polar family."

The acquisition builds on Empresas Polar's more than 15-year presence in the United States. In 2010, the company acquired its first U.S. production facility in Florida to produce beer and malt beverages for North America and the Caribbean. In 2014, it opened its International Grains and Cereals plant in Greenville, Texas, to support the growth of its P.A.N. brand across the region. Today, Empresas Polar has a presence in several U.S. food and beverage categories, including precooked corn flour, mixes, frozen foods, mayonnaise, milk modifiers, and malt beverages. This growth and success in the U.S. market has allowed Empresas Polar to identify new portfolio options, paving the way for the acquisition of Ricos Products.

BofA Securities acted as exclusive financial advisor and Norton Rose Fulbright acted as legal advisor to Ricos. Balandra Capital acted as financial advisor and Skadden acted as legal advisor to Empresas Polar.

"Ricos began with a simple idea at a Texas ballpark and grew into a beloved brand with a following around the world," added Mendoza. "We look forward to building on that remarkable history, working alongside the Ricos team and the San Antonio community to create new opportunities for growth."

About Empresas Polar
Founded in Caracas, Venezuela, in 1941, Empresas Polar is a family-owned food and beverage company now led by the third generation of the Mendoza family. Its portfolio includes iconic brands such as Harina P.A.N., Cerveza Polar, and Maltín Polar, with operations spanning Venezuela, Colombia, the United States, Spain, and other international markets. Polar is the PepsiCo bottler in Venezuela and Mexico through a joint venture. Alimentos Polar International, Inc. is a subsidiary of Empresas Polar.

data.title: Slower wage growth curbs US labor costs in third quarter
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US labor costs increased moderately in the third quarter amid a slowdown in wage growth, suggesting that the labor market was unlikely to be an inflation risk.

The economy is struggling with rising price pressures, mostly stemming from the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran, which has raised the cost of energy goods and fertilizers, as well as an AI investment boom. The Federal Reserve on Wednesday left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated." Economists expect the US central bank to raise borrowing costs in December.  

"Labor-cost inflation continues to move in the right direction," said Priscilla Thiagamoorthy, a senior economist at BMO Capital Markets. "While consumer inflation remains elevated, the Fed will take some comfort from the fact that the labor market is no longer a significant source of price pressures."

The Employment Cost Index (ECI), the broadest measure of labor costs, rose 0.8% last quarter after increasing 0.9% in the April-June period, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Friday. The increase in the ECI was in line with economists' expectations.

Labor costs advanced 3.4% in the 12 months through September after rising by the same margin in the year through June. The ECI is viewed by policymakers as one of the better measures of labor market slack and a predictor of core inflation because it adjusts for composition and changes in job quality.

Wages and salaries, which account for the bulk of labor costs, climbed 0.7% last quarter after rising 0.9% in the second quarter. In the 12 months through September, wages increased 3.1%, mostly lagging inflation. They had advanced 3.2% in the year through June. 

The government reported on Thursday that the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index shot up 3.6% year-on-year in September. Core PCE inflation, which excludes the volatile food and energy components, increased 3.1% on a year-on-year basis in September. These two measures are tracked by the Fed for its 2% inflation target. 

INFLATION-ADJUSTED WAGES FALL AGAIN

The BLS report showed wages adjusted for inflation dropped 0.6% in the 12 months through September after declining 0.3% in the year through June. Economists said this underscored what they called a cost of living crisis that was depressing consumer sentiment and tanking President Donald Trump's approval rating.

"Paychecks are barely able to keep workers' heads above water, trying to scratch out a living," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "Bringing home a real paycheck that matches inflation is next to impossible for most Americans. No wonder consumer confidence remains on the low side of life."

Public sector wages climbed 0.6% last quarter after gaining 0.9% in the April-June period. They advanced 3.2% in the 12 months through September.

data.title: Intel on course for worst day ever, triggers global chip rout
data.description:
By Anhata Rooprai

Oct 30 (Reuters) - Intel ( INTC ) tumbled 29% on Friday and was on track for its sharpest one-day decline, deepening a broader retreat in technology stocks as investors grew increasingly wary of weakening PC demand and the vast spending required to build out AI infrastructure.

The steep fall put the US chipmaker on track to shed more than $137 billion in market value, underscoring the challenges facing CEO Lip-Bu Tan's turnaround as a prolonged PC slump offsets heavy investments in AI and manufacturing expansion.

Semiconductor stocks, including Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Arm Holdings, Qualcomm ( QCOM ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Micron, fell between 2% and 10%.

"The market is in a sell first, ask questions later mood right now, and Intel's ( INTC ) warning has given investors an easy excuse to take some money off the table across chip stocks," said Matt Britzman, senior equity analyst, Hargreaves Lansdown.

The selloff spread to server makers, reflecting investor caution toward companies tied to the semiconductor and AI infrastructure supply chain.

Shares of server makers Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Super Micro Computer fell between 6% and 10%.

The STOXX Europe 600 Technology Index fell 2%, with sector heavyweight ASML shedding 4.6%. US-listed shares of TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, fell 3.3%.

Intel ( INTC ) forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $17.07 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Finance chief David Zinsner also said Intel ( INTC ) does not expect positive cash flow this year.

MEMORY CRUNCH BITES

Higher memory prices, driven by suppliers shifting capacity toward AI-focused high-bandwidth memory chips, are raising PC costs and weighing on already weak consumer demand.

PC chips accounted for roughly half of Intel's ( INTC ) third-quarter revenue, and the company expects sales from the segment to decline more than 20% sequentially this quarter after a 5% drop in the September period.

"It will be important to see if Intel ( INTC ) can expand the highly profitable Xeon product supply to help offset this developing weakness in PC," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management.

"Bottom line, weaker sales volumes, higher manufacturing costs, and an out-of-cycle product mix is a recipe for the stock to decline over the near term as future earnings are under a lot of pressure."

(Reporting by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, additional reporting by Sudeshna Ghoshal; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX set for second weekly decline as gold slump, tech weakness weigh
data.description:
By Anand Gopal R

Oct 30 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index hit a one-week low on Friday, dragged down by declines in mining and technology stocks, as lower gold prices and concerns over growing AI costs hit sentiment.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index was down 1.57% at 35,673.99 points as of 10:33 a.m. ET (1433 GMT), putting the index on track for a second straight weekly loss.

Eight out of the 10 main TSX sectors were trading lower.

* The materials sector, which includes miners, fell 4.9% to a nearly two-month low

* Gold prices retreated 2% to their lowest level since November 2025, as rising crude oil prices and persistent inflation concerns reinforced expectations of further US interest rate hikes

* The technology sector fell 2.6%, mirroring declines in Wall Street, after Amazon ( AMZN ) posted a sharp third-quarter cash burn, while Intel ( INTC ) warned of more cash burn this year amid a weak PC market

* Heavily weighted financials shed 1.2% and industrials fell 0.5%, adding to the losses on the index

* On the data front, Canada's economy stalled in August for the second straight month as strength in the retail, manufacturing and construction sectors was largely offset by a drop in activity in wholesale trade and public administration

* Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones, said oil dynamics remained very uncertain because of the Middle East conflict and that Canada's GDP, which came in below expectations, "potentially suggest that the Bank of Canada (BoC) should proceed cautiously when it comes to raising rates"

* The BoC hiked interest rates at its meeting earlier this week and is widely expected to hold interest rates steady at its December meeting, according to LSEG data

* The energy sector was among the few bright spots in the index, rising 0.7% on higher oil prices

* Among individual movers, uranium producer Cameco ( CCJ ) was the largest loser on the index, sliding 9.5% after missing third-quarter revenue estimates

data.title: US STOCKS-Nasdaq hits near three-month low as Amazon, Intel deepen AI capex concerns
data.description:
* Indexes down: Dow 0.39%, S&P 500 1.22%, Nasdaq 2.21%

* Intel ( INTC ) slides after reporting big cash burn

* Alphabet extends losses a day after record selloff

(Updates for market open)

By Shashwat Chauhan and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Oct 30 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq tumbled to its lowest in nearly three months on Friday after Amazon's ( AMZN ) aggressive AI spending plan and Intel's ( INTC ) cash burn warning intensified concerns over mounting costs of AI infrastructure buildout and the timeline for returns.

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) slipped 2% after the company reported a sharp cash outflow in the third quarter and signaled another increase in capital expenditure next year, on top of already elevated outlays. It pared much of its premarket declines.

Intel ( INTC ) tanked more than 30%, set for its biggest one-day loss on record, after the chipmaker warned it would burn cash this year due to a weak market for personal computers, manufacturing hurdles and heavy spending to expand production.

The decline sparked a selloff in global chip stocks, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) down 3% and AMD sliding 9.3%. The broader chips index shed 5.7%. Server makers Dell and HP lost about 9% each.

Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) were set to wipe out about $200 billion in combined market value, if losses hold, putting the Nasdaq-100 on track to erase just over $1 trillion. The index is set to shed over $2 trillion this month.

"It's more a question of what is priced into a stock and how much investors are expecting. Alphabet, Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) fall into the category where it doesn't take much to trigger a significant disappointment," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.

"I don't think this is a broader reset... It's more of a rotation out of an extremely popular technology trade and into safer havens."

Consumer staples and healthcare indexes, traditionally considered defensive sectors, were up 1.9% and 1.7%, respectively.

The S&P 500 information technology index was the biggest drag, down 3.4% and set for its biggest one-day fall since June 23. The communication services index lost 0.7% and was headed for its worst month since April 2022.

Alphabet slipped 1.2%, after a record selloff in the previous session when the Google parent reported disappointing results in its search-advertising business and a sharp increase in cash outflows.

Microsoft ( MSFT ), however delivered a big cash-flow beat, though it raised $25 billion through a debt sale.

At 09:53 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 203.15 points, or 0.39%, to 52,139.41. The S&P 500 lost 94.01 points, or 1.22%, to 7,626.38, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 578.39 points, or 2.21%, to 25,606.33.

Energy stocks were supported by a 1.7% and 2.7% gain in Chevron ( CVX ) and Exxon Mobil, respectively, after they beat third-quarter profit estimates.

All three indexes were on course for weekly losses. While the Dow was on track for monthly gains, the Nasdaq was set to snap a two-month winning streak in October.

Expectations that the US Federal Reserve, according to LSEG data, would raise interest rates by more than 50 basis points by mid-2027, added to AI capex concerns as companies increasingly rely on debt to fund their buildout, and higher borrowing costs could make such spending harder to justify.

The central bank held rates steady earlier this week, as expected.

Among other movers, social media platform Reddit ( RDDT ) slid 26% after CEO Steve Huffman warned that total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.31-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by 2.4-to-1 on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 39 new 52-week highs and four new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 51 new highs and 160 new lows.

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips and Shilpi Majumdar)

data.title: PRECIOUS-Gold hits one-year low, silver drops below $50 as higher-for-longer rate view firms
data.description:
* Bullion on track for 5.9% decline in October

* Silver falls below $50/oz for the first time since November 2025

* Precious metals on track for second straight monthly decline

(Updates for US morning session)

By Noel John

Oct 30 (Reuters) - Gold fell to a one-year low on Friday and silver slid below $50 an ounce for the first time since November 2025 as higher energy prices and persistent inflation concerns strengthened expectations that US interest rates will stay high.

Spot gold was down 2.7% at $3,910.53 per ounce by 10:05 a.m. ET (1405 GMT), its lowest since October 2025.

US gold futures for December delivery fell 2.8% to $3,919.60 per ounce. Bullion prices are on track for a second straight monthly decline, down 5.9% so far this month.

Spot silver was down 5.8% at $49.34 per ounce, its lowest since November 2025.

"Ongoing concerns about inflation have multiple central banks continuing to tilt hawkish," said Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals.

"Even though holds were delivered by major central banks this week, the indication was that the higher-for-longer theme prevails, and that's weighing on precious metals."

Major central banks hit pause on rate rises this week, but made clear the tightening cycle isn't over, with the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank both pointing to inflation risks from surging energy costs.

Data on Thursday showed US inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for gasoline and other goods, bolstering economists' expectations of a rate hike in December.

Another factor for the price decline is the sharp fall in technology stock prices, which may have led to forced selling and margin calls, analysts at Commerzbank said in a note.

"We consider the fall in precious metal prices to be exaggerated and continue to expect a recovery," they added.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq was set for steep losses at Friday's open on AI spending worries.

Meanwhile, oil prices climbed and were set for a fourth monthly gain. Higher energy prices strengthen expectations of a prolonged period of elevated interest rates, making non-yielding assets such as gold less attractive.

Elsewhere, physical gold demand in key Asian markets remained subdued this week, with Indian buyers delaying purchases in anticipation of a further decline in prices, while demand in top consumer China stayed muted.

Platinum dropped 4% to $1,428.35, its lowest since September 2025, and palladium fell 3.1% to $975.25, its lowest since June 2025. Both were poised for weekly and monthly declines.

(Reporting by Noel John in Bengaluru; Editing by Jan Harvey)

data.title: Colgate-Palmolive Lifts Full-Year Earnings Growth Outlook Following Third-Quarter Beat
data.description:
10:33 AM EDT, 10/30/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Colgate-Palmolive ( CL ) raised its full-year earnings growth outlook on Friday as the consumer products company reported better-than-expected third-quarter results amid volume and price gains.

The company now anticipates per-share adjusted earnings to rise by 5% to 7% for 2026, up from its previous projections for a mid-single-digit increase. The current consensus on FactSet is for non-GAAP EPS of $3.86.

Colgate-Palmolive's ( CL ) shares rose 2.4% in Friday trade. The stock is up 21% year to date.

Sales are pegged to grow by 4% to 5% for the ongoing year, compared with the prior guidance for a 2% to 6% advance. The Street is looking for an increase of 5.1%.

"Raw material, packaging and logistics costs remain elevated, driven by the conflict in the Middle East, which has increased oil prices as well as other commodity costs," Colgate-Palmolive's ( CL ) management said in prepared remarks. "We are broadly locked in for the remainder of the year based on our cost projections, which may differ from spot prices."

For the September quarter, the company's adjusted EPS improved to $0.97 from $0.91 the year before, topping the average analyst estimate of $0.93. Sales inclined 4.6% to $5.37 billion, just ahead of the Street's view for $5.34 billion. On an organic basis, sales were up 3.6% year over year.

Earlier this week, RBC Capital Markets said it expected Colgate-Palmolive ( CL ) to report quarterly results in line with estimates and reiterate its full-year guidance. The firm said it did not expect a material change in the narrative surrounding the company's North American business, where tracked consumption trends remained soft.

The company's overall volume increased 1.7% amid gains across all regions except North America, where the metric slid 3.7%. Overall pricing climbed 2%.

Organic sales improved sequentially in North America but were impacted by continued softness in the US, Colgate-Palmolive ( CL ) said in the prepared remarks. The US market backdrop remains challenging amid volatile consumer behavior and weak sentiment due to rising fuel prices, but the company saw early signs of improvement in the toothpaste market share in the quarter, it said.

Sales in the oral, personal and home care segment moved higher to $4.16 billion from $3.99 billion in the 2025 quarter, while the pet nutrition business ticked up to $1.21 billion from $1.14 billion.

data.title: AstraZeneca CEO strikes bullish tone on pipeline as stock rallies
data.description:
* Aims for $1.5 billion in annual savings over three years

* Plan involves up to $2 billion in one-time restructuring charges

* Third-quarter sales and profit top analysts' expectations

* Shares up nearly 6%, erasing year-to-date losses

(Adds detail from media call in paragraphs 4-5. Updates shares)

By Pushkala Aripaka and Patrick Wingrove

Oct 30 (Reuters) - AstraZeneca ( AZN ) unveiled plans on Friday to save about $1.5 billion annually to invest in its drug pipeline, sparking the biggest one-day share rally in a year as CEO Pascal Soriot moved to shift the focus back to growth after a turbulent few months.

The more bullish tone signals a revival for the UK-based drugmaker, a long-term market success story, which saw some clinical trial setbacks and talk of a deal for smaller US rival Bristol Myers Squibb ( BMY ) weigh on its shares earlier in the year.

"With multiple potential blockbuster assets in late-stage development and transformative technologies scaling rapidly, we are on track to deliver our 2030 ambition and to sustain growth through the next decade," Soriot said in a statement.

AstraZeneca ( AZN ) gave few details of how it will make the savings. On a press call, executives said some departments face cutbacks or restructuring, while others will re-skill and hire for emerging needs. Soriot said shifting focus from patent-expiring drugs such as Farxiga and Brilinta to oncology and rare diseases could render some R&D roles redundant.

Although executives withheld specific employment and geographic targets, they said the company would experience net job growth across different areas.

AstraZeneca ( AZN ) shares were up about 6% by 1433 GMT, having risen as much as 7.3% earlier in the day. They are on track to reverse losses from earlier in the year.

The company also beat third-quarter sales and profit forecasts, and maintained its 2026 outlook.

"These results should reassure investors after a turbulent period for what historically has been a really strong business," said Quilter Cheviot analyst Sheena Berry.

AstraZeneca ( AZN ) is increasing investment across its business as Soriot seeks to convince investors the company remains on track to achieve its target of $80 billion in annual revenue by 2030 despite recent clinical trial setbacks. The target relies in part on more than 25 blockbuster medicines.

RESTRUCTURING PLAN

The company said savings from the three-year programme would be reinvested mainly in its pipeline of more than 180 projects, but that it expected to incur up to $2 billion in one-off restructuring charges.

Drugmakers are facing growing investor scrutiny over the strength of their pipelines as patents expire on established blockbuster medicines and future growth becomes increasingly dependent on successful late-stage trial results.

British rival GSK is also pursuing a cost-saving programme.

Questions over AstraZeneca's ( AZN ) pipeline intensified following setbacks involving camizestrant and Wainua. However, investors have generally remained confident that the breadth of the company's late-stage portfolio leaves it well placed to absorb disappointments.

THIRD-QUARTER BEAT

Core earnings for the quarter were $2.79 per share as revenue rose 7% at constant exchange rates to $16.21 billion, beating analysts' forecasts of $2.59 per share and $15.94 billion respectively.

Growth was driven by cancer and rare-disease medicines. Oncology revenue rose 17% to $7.77 billion, helped by a 35% jump in Enhertu sales to $969 million and a 26% rise in Imfinzi sales to about $2 billion.

The gains helped offset pressure from older products facing generic competition. Sales of diabetes drug Farxiga fell 25% to $1.61 billion.

AstraZeneca ( AZN ) reported operating expenses of $27.56 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 7% from a year earlier. It said costs would rise again in the fourth quarter in line with seasonal trends.

With 2026 guidance unchanged, analysts said investor attention is increasingly turning to 2027, when AstraZeneca ( AZN ) expects a series of late-stage trial results that it says could generate more than $20 billion in peak annual sales.

($1 = 0.7481 pounds)

(Reporting by Pushkala Aripaka, Sri Hari N S in Bengaluru and Patrick Wingrove in London; Editing by Joe Bavier, Mark Potter and Jan Harvey)

data.title: Sanofi teases appetite for larger deals, lifts 2026 growth targets under new CEO Garijo
data.description:
By Bhanvi Satija

LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - French drugmaker Sanofi said on Friday it was prepared to pursue larger deals as it seeks to rebuild its basket of experimental drugs for future growth under new CEO Belen Garijo.

Its shares rose nearly 6% to their highest since April and were among the top gainers in Europe as the company raised its 2026 growth targets for the second time this year.

Garijo, who took the top role in May, is tasked with charting Sanofi's growth trajectory post the early 2030s, when its blockbuster asthma drug Dupixent loses patent exclusivity.

On Friday, finance chief Francois Roger said the company was increasingly interested in deals that would give it access to late-stage medicines or marketed products, and would consider acquisitions larger than its usual range of $2 billion to $5 billion.

"These assets are more expensive," he told journalists after third-quarter results.

He said Sanofi will stick to areas where it already operates - immunology, rare diseases and vaccines.

"We could consider potentially what we call white spaces or moonshots with unmet medical needs," Roger added.

NEW CEO HAS PROMISED FASTER DECISION-MAKING

Garijo has kicked off a strategic review and promised investors faster decision-making since taking over. She also overhauled her executive committee to expand Roger's role to include business development, and hired former Roche executive Paulo Fontoura to lead R&D.

"We are fully committed to executing on our plan and moving with the necessary sense of urgency," Garijo said on a call with analysts.

She said Sanofi will keep moving at its current pace and will give more details on medium- to long-term priorities before year-end.

Analysts estimate that Sanofi has about €20 billion to spend on deals, and believe it will need to use some of that before a raft of late-stage trial data is expected in 2027.

"Management has understood the urgency of the situation and Belen is acting fast," said Markus Manns, a portfolio manager at Sanofi shareholder Union Investment.

Sanofi earlier this month entered into an expanded partnership with US partner Regeneron, worth up to $8 billion, to develop four new drugs together and settle prior litigation.

"Short term, I am focused on a potential M&A transaction, which I assume will come rather sooner than later," Manns said, adding that he will closely watch for details from Fontoura on his plans for rebuilding the internal pipeline.

OUTLOOK LIFTED, THIRD QUARTER BEATS FORECASTS

The company said it now expects sales and profit per share this year to grow by a low-teens and mid-teens percentage, respectively, helped by strong sales of Dupixent and cost management.

Previously, it had expected sales growth of 10% at a constant exchange rate, and profit per share to grow slightly faster than sales. At least three analysts said the raise would lift market consensus for Sanofi's full-year earnings.

The company is focused on "returns rather than restructuring," Roger said, adding that Sanofi is investing heavily in artificial intelligence for R&D, which it expects could cut some development timelines.

Sanofi has identified areas where it can move faster and execute better, he said, and is working through simplifying processes and governance.

The French drugmaker posted third-quarter business operating income, a profit metric, of €5.43 billion, compared with market expectations of €4.32 billion.

Profit was helped by a larger share of sales from its newer launches, including hemophilia A treatment ALTUVIIIO, as well as better prices after discounts.

Total sales were €14.44 billion, up 14.3% at constant exchange rates, ahead of a €13.25 billion analyst estimate. Dupixent sales reached €5.69 billion, about 10% above expectations.

(Reporting by Bhanvi Satija in London; Editing by Elaine Hardcastle and Jan Harvey)
